Recall that, if $F=P\,\text{i}+Q\,\text{j}$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2},$ then the following are equivalent:

* $F$ is a source-free vector field.

* $∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.$

* The flux ${∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s$ along any closed curve $C\in D$ is zero.

* Flux is path-independent. That is, given two curves ${C}_{1},{C}_{2}\in D$ with the same start and end points, we have that

$$
{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s.
$$

* There exists a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ for $F.$

First, for our vector field $F=({x}^{2}-2{y}^{2})\,\text{i}-2xy\,\text{j}$, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-2{y}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2xy) \\  & =2x-2x \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $F$ is a source-free vector field. So, the flux of $F$ across any closed curve is zero. Hence,

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s=0.
$$
